empty.title: Add your first host
empty.text: Vigie connects to your servers over SSH with the keys you already use, and runs WP-CLI there. Nothing is installed on your sites.

detail.select: Select a folder, host or site.

cli.usage:
Usage: vigie [--data-dir <dir>] [command]

Without a command, Vigie opens its window.

Commands:
  tree [--json]                   Print the site manager with each site's status
  scan [path] [--check-files] [--json]
                                  Scan a site, a host or a folder (everything without a path);
                                  --check-files compares the files again, even within the day
  discover <host path> [--json]   List the WordPress installs of a host (adds nothing)
  update [path] [--yes] [--json]  Preview, then update a site, a host or a folder (asks first)
  export [path] [--history] [-o <file>] [--json]
                                  Export everything, a folder or a host (to the standard output
                                  without -o); --history adds the scans, updates and rollbacks
  import <file> [--into <folder>] [--yes] [--trust-keys] [--json]
  import --ssh-config [--into <folder>] [--yes] [--json]
                                  Preview, then add what is new from an export, a CSV site list
                                  or ~/.ssh/config (asks first); host keys are kept only once
                                  confirmed, or with --trust-keys
  version                         Print the version
  help                            Print this help

Paths name folders, hosts and sites: "Clients/Infomaniak/misits.ch".
Exit status: 0 all good, 1 needs attention or not fully checked, 2 urgent, 3 error.

cli.truncated_one: More installs were found: only the first {{count}} was checked.

update.rollbackHint: Roll back from the window: the History tab of the site.
update.jsonNeedsYes: --json needs --yes: a script cannot answer the confirmation

export.sensitive: The file names your servers and SSH users, and holds your notes: keep it somewhere safe.
export.notExportable: a site is exported with its host: give the path of the host, of a folder, or none for everything

import.needsFile: import needs one file, an export or a CSV site list, or --ssh-config
import.jsonNeedsYes: --json needs --yes: a script cannot answer the confirmation
import.notAnExport: {{file}} is neither a Vigie export nor a CSV site list
import.newer: this export was written by a newer Vigie: update Vigie to import it
import.top: the top of the site manager

reason.same-name: the folder of that name receives what the file puts in it
reason.same-connection: a host reaches the same account

line.columns: not as many values as the header
line.no-connection: neither an alias nor a host
line.bad-port: a port that is not one
line.bad-name: a name that is empty or has a slash
line.bad-folder: a folder path with an empty part
line.other-folder: its account is in another folder on an earlier line

import.history: With the sites added: {{ignores}} findings set aside, {{scans}} scans, {{operations}} updates and rollbacks.
import.keyOffered: Key of {{host}}: {{type}} {{fingerprint}}, trusted only if you confirm it.
import.keyRefused: Key of {{host}} not kept: {{reason}}. The host asks at its first connection.

key.invalid: it is not a valid key
key.unresolved: ssh does not resolve the alias here
key.other-trusted: Vigie trusts another key for this server

import.trustPrompt: Trust {{type}} {{fingerprint}} for {{host}}? Check it with its administrator. [y/N]
import.keysLeft: The keys not confirmed were not kept: those hosts ask at their first connection.

outcome.notWordPress: No WordPress at this path any more: the folder is empty or gone. If the site left this server, remove it from Vigie too.

failure.unresolved: The host name could not be found. Check the address.
failure.refused: The server refused the connection on this port. Check the port, and that SSH is enabled for this account.
failure.timedOut: The server did not answer. Some hosts only accept SSH from allowed IP addresses (o2switch, for example): allow yours in the host's control panel.
failure.hostKeyUnknown: The server's key is not trusted yet. Add the host again to check and trust its fingerprint.
failure.hostKeyChanged: The server's key has changed since it was trusted. It can be a server change or an attack: check with the host before trusting the new key.
failure.authRefused: The server refused the key. Is it loaded in your SSH agent (Bitwarden, 1Password, ssh-agent)?
failure.keyFileMissing: The key file set for this host does not exist.
failure.unreadable: Vigie could not read the answer of WP-CLI: this WordPress or WP-CLI answers in a way Vigie does not know yet.

problem.slashInName: A name cannot contain a slash.
problem.noConnection: Enter an SSH alias, or a host name and a user.
problem.invalidPort: The port must be between 1 and 65535.
problem.duplicateName: This name is already used here.
problem.keyNotReceived: This key was not received from the server. Ask for the keys again.
problem.noPhp: PHP does not run on the command line of this account: {{message}}
problem.noWpCli: WP-CLI was not found on this account (tried: {{message}}).
problem.findFailed: The search for WordPress installs failed: {{message}}
problem.notFound: This item no longer exists: the list was changed meanwhile.
problem.siteMoved: A site stays under its host. If it moved to another account, delete it here and use "Find new sites" on that host.
problem.folderNotEmpty: Only an empty folder can be deleted: move or delete what it holds first.
problem.moveIntoItself: A folder cannot go into itself or one of its folders.
problem.busy: An update or a rollback already runs on this site: wait for its end.
problem.noDumpTool: The server has no database dump tool (mariadb-dump or mysqldump), and Vigie dumps the database before every update.
problem.previewFirst: Look at the preview of the update first: it may have changed.
problem.notOffered: This item is not in the preview any more: look at it again.
problem.nothingToRollBack: There is nothing to roll back.
problem.reasonRequired: A reason is required to ignore a finding permanently.
problem.unknownDestination: Vigie does not know this service.
problem.scanning: This site is being scanned: wait for the scan to end before updating it.
problem.notAnExport: This file is not a Vigie export.
problem.newerExport: This export was written by a newer Vigie: update Vigie to import it.
problem.invalidExport: This export does not hold together and cannot be imported: {{message}}
problem.notACSV: This file is not a site list Vigie reads: {{message}}
problem.notExportable: A site is exported with its host: export the host or a folder.
problem.noImport: No import is being previewed: choose the file again.
problem.notAFolder: Sites can only be imported into a folder.
problem.keyChanged: Vigie trusts another key for one of these servers since the preview: look at the preview again.
problem.importChanged: The site manager changed since the preview: look at the preview again.
problem.sshConfigDepth: ~/.ssh/config includes files in a loop, or too deep.

lead.connection: A host is one SSH account. Vigie uses the keys of your SSH agent and never asks for a password.
lead.key: First connection to {{host}}. Compare this fingerprint with the one your host publishes before trusting it.
lead.test: Vigie checks the connection, PHP on the command line and WP-CLI, then searches the account for WordPress installs. Nothing is written on the server.
lead.sites_one: {{count}} WordPress install found in the account. Vigie adds only the ones you check.
lead.sites_other: {{count}} WordPress installs found in the account. Vigie adds only the ones you check.

mode.hostText: As your host gives them, for example in its control panel.
mode.aliasText: An entry you already use in the terminal.

field.name: Name in Vigie
field.keyPathHint: Optional: only this key is offered
field.keyPathPlaceholder: The keys of my SSH agent

wizard.compared: I compared this fingerprint with the one of my host
wizard.keyWhere: Vigie keeps it in its own known_hosts; your SSH files are not changed.

progress.keys: Asking the server for its keys…
progress.search: Searching the account for WordPress installs…
progress.adding: Adding the host and its sites…

overview.unchecked: not checked: wordpress.org could not be reached
overview.sourceUnknownHint: Not on wordpress.org; their own updater does not run during a scan.
overview.neverScanned: This site has not been scanned yet.
overview.scanProblem: The last scan did not complete
overview.attemptTitle: The latest scan did not complete
overview.attemptText: {{reason}}. These results are from the scan of {{date}} at {{time}}.

move.title: Move "{{name}}"
move.leadHost: Choose the folder that will hold it. Its sites go with it.
move.leadFolder: Choose the folder that will hold it, with everything in it.

delete.leadHost_one: Its site, its scans and its update history are removed from Vigie.
delete.leadHost_other: Its {{count}} sites, their scans and their update history are removed from Vigie.
delete.leadSite: Its scans and its update history are removed from Vigie.
delete.notEmpty: Only an empty folder can be deleted: move or delete what it holds first.
delete.keep: Nothing changes on the server: the sites, and the backups Vigie made in ~/.vigie, stay there.

host.title: Edit the connection
host.lead_one: {{name}} and its site use these settings.
host.lead_other: {{name}} and its {{count}} sites use these settings.
host.addressChanged: The address changed: once saved, Vigie asks {{host}} for its key, for you to check it.
host.maxInvalid: A whole number from 1 to 10, or empty for 2.

key.title: Check the key of {{host}}
key.lead: The address of the host changed. Compare this fingerprint with the one your host publishes before trusting it.

find.title: Find new sites
find.lead: WordPress installs of {{name}}. Vigie adds only the ones you check.
find.none: No new install on this account.

edit.dropAtRoot: Drop to move {{name}} to the top level
edit.renameHint: Enter keeps the name, Escape cancels
edit.emptyFolder: No site in this folder yet.
edit.emptyHost: No site on this host yet: "Find new sites…" in its menu searches the account.

notOffered.unavailable: Not offered: needs a newer PHP or WordPress

preview.title: Update {{name}}
preview.lead: Vigie backs up first, then updates one item at a time and checks the site after each one. It stops at the first problem.
preview.loading: Vigie reads on the server what will change.
preview.backupsFirst: Backed up first, on the server
preview.where: Kept with the last 3 updates of this site, in a folder outside the web root:
preview.coreText: The site shows the maintenance page of WordPress for about a minute. If you roll back afterwards, the database returns to its state before the update: orders or comments written in between are lost.
preview.nothing: Nothing you chose is offered any more: the site may have been updated in the meantime.

run.title: Updating {{name}}
run.lead: You can close this window: the update goes on, and the site list shows it.
run.notStarted: Vigie could not start this update. Scan the site, then try again.

result.doneLead: Each item was checked after its update.
result.failedLead: The update stopped at the first problem: nothing else was started.
result.failedOn: {{item}}: the site no longer passes the checks
result.rollbackFiles: Roll back puts the folder of {{item}} back as it was, then checks the site again. The database is not touched: only a WordPress update restores it.
result.rollbackCore: Roll back puts the WordPress files and the database back as they were before the update, then checks the site again.
result.nothingToRollBack: No item was changed: there is nothing to put back.
result.cancelledLead: The items already updated stay so; the next ones were not started.
result.interruptedLead: Vigie was closed during the update. Scan the site to see where it stands.
result.rolledBackLead: {{item}} is back to its earlier version, and the site passes the checks again.
result.rollbackFailedLead: The site is not as it was. The backup stays on the server:

step.rescanDetail: versions read again on the server, older backups removed

bulk.stoppedText: An item broke this site: open it to roll back or keep the new version. The next sites of the same host were not started.
bulk.notStarted: An earlier site of the same host failed, or the update was stopped

bulkDialog.title: Update everything in {{name}}
bulkDialog.lead: The sites of a host go one after another, each backed up and checked as on its own; a host stops at its first broken site.
bulkDialog.loading: Vigie reads on the server what each site will change.

security.notScanned: Scan the site to see its security.

consent.title: Before the first security scan
consent.lead: To find known vulnerabilities, closed plugins and expiry dates, Vigie asks a few services from your computer. This is exactly what each one receives. Nothing is sent until you agree.
consent.later: You can change these choices at any time in Settings.

settings.lookupsLead: What Vigie asks, from your computer, during a security scan. A lookup turned off leaves its checks “not checked”, never “up to date”.
settings.services: Services asked during a security scan
settings.agreedDesc: Given on {{date}} at {{time}}. Withdrawing it stops every lookup outside; those checks become “not checked”.
settings.notAgreedDesc: Not given: nothing is sent, and the checks that need it are “not checked”.
